summary:
SEVEN ASSIGNED ITEMS, ALL SEVEN CLOSED, by three new refusals: a non-finite refusal over every
float lever in src/opt/api.py::build, a non-finite refusal plus a probability-interval refusal over
TOK_DROPOUT in src/tok/api.py::build_vocabulary, and a floor of two on TOK_MAX_BYTES in the same
function. One report defect fixed alongside them (the grad_clip Gate's hardcoded "off (0.0)").
FOUR FILES CHANGED, ALL FOUR MINE. Nothing under tests/, runs/ or docs/ touched.

=====================================================================================
WHAT SHAPE THE ELEVEN OPT REFUSALS COLLECTIVELY HAVE -- THE ANSWER THE BRIEF ASKED FOR
=====================================================================================
The eleven `raise` statements in OPT.build cover TEN levers (lr_restart_damp has two). Read as
grammar rather than as intent, they are two families and the split is exactly the sweep's:

  NINE ARE ONE-SIDED ORDER COMPARISONS naming ONE side of a boundary:
      damp > 1.0 | damp < 0.0 | lr <= 0.0 | weight_decay < 0.0 | warmup_asked < 0 |
      wavelength_asked < 0 | n_accum < 1 | n_batch_windows < 1 | grad_clip < 0.0
  TWO ARE INVERTED CHAINS naming an interval at BOTH ends:
      not 0.0 <= min_frac < 1.0 | not 0.0 <= decay <= 1.0

NaN is ordered against nothing, so it is False for every one of the nine and True for both of the
two. +inf passes every lower bound. -inf is caught by seven of the nine INCIDENTALLY -- because it
happens to be negative, by guards written about sign, not about reality. MEASURED before the change,
one lever per fresh subprocess (matrix in the repro field of each finding):
  OPT_LR:              nan BUILT-then-torch, inf BUILT, -inf refused, 1e30 BUILT
  OPT_WEIGHT_DECAY:    nan BUILT-then-torch, inf BUILT, -inf refused, 1e30 BUILT
  OPT_GRAD_CLIP:       nan BUILT, inf BUILT, -inf refused, 1e30 BUILT
  OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP: nan BUILT, inf refused, -inf refused, 1e30 refused
  OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC / OPT_LR_DECAY: all four refused
So counted by LEVER rather than by statement: THREE of the six float levers were bounded on both
sides and THREE on one side only -- and of the three bounded on both sides, the two written as
inverted chains ALSO held against NaN while the one written as two separate one-sided tests
(lr_restart_damp) did not. The two that held held BY GRAMMAR, not by intent. That is the shape:
NINE STATEMENTS THAT SAY WHICH SIDE IS ILLEGAL, TWO THAT SAY WHAT THE DOMAIN IS.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF, MEASURED. The brief says every one of the eleven passes inf. Two do
not: OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC and OPT_LR_DECAY are refused at nan, +inf, -inf AND 1e30 by their inverted
chains, and OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP is refused at +inf and at 1e30 by `damp > 1.0`. And OPT_LR=nan /
OPT_WEIGHT_DECAY=nan were NOT refused by OPT.build at all -- they walked all eleven, the horizon was
resolved and printed, and the run died in torch's AdamW constructor with `ValueError: Invalid
learning rate: nan`, naming no lever, no environment variable and no package.

=====================================================================================
WHAT LANDED
=====================================================================================
(1) src/opt/api.py::build -- A TWELFTH REFUSAL, FIRST IN THE BODY, over every float lever OPT
    declares, enumerated through spine/lever.py::Config.keys and ::Config.lever so the env name in
    the message is GENERATED and a float lever added tomorrow is covered with no second list to go
    stale (precedent: src/fabric/api.py::build). Six float levers x 3 values = 18 cells, every one
    now LeverError naming the lever and the value, each quoting its own measurement out of a new
    module-level _NONFINITE_MEASURED table. The other seven declarations are accounted for and not
    declined: five int levers refused at nan (ValueError) and +/-inf (OverflowError) by
    spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce under their owned names, one bool, one str with choices=.
    6 + 5 + 1 + 1 = 13, the whole set.
(2) src/opt/api.py::counters -- the opt.build.grad_clip Gate now INTERPOLATES the resolved value in
    both its `value` and its `reason`. Both were the literal 0.0, and `clip > 0.0` is False for NaN
    as well as for zero, so at OPT_GRAD_CLIP=nan the ledger printed value='off (0.0)' beside the
    sentence "OPT_GRAD_CLIP=0.0 is OFF, which is the setting every recorded number in this project
    was taken under" -- one line above a second gate in the SAME ledger printing "OPT_GRAD_CLIP=nan
    is OFF". A report asserting a value the operator did not type, contradicting itself.
(3) src/tok/api.py::build_vocabulary -- THREE refusals at the first read, before the Vocabulary is
    constructed (row 11 of spine/compose.py::ASSEMBLY_ORDER, TOK's first entry point): non-finite
    over all four float levers (same introspection, same shape, its own _NONFINITE_MEASURED table);
    TOK_DROPOUT outside [0.0, 1.0], written as the inverted chain because that is the grammar NaN
    does not walk through; and TOK_MAX_BYTES below 2.
(4) src/opt/levers.py and src/tok/levers.py -- the measurement and the refusal recorded beside the
    declarations of grad_clip, max_bytes and dropout, each with what is NOT closed.

=====================================================================================
WHAT THESE REFUSALS DO NOT CLAIM, AND NO DOCSTRING IN THE DIFF SAYS OTHERWISE
=====================================================================================
They close FOUR VALUES per float lever, the finite values outside ONE declared probability
interval, and two counts. THEY BOUND NOTHING and neither package is thereby safe, validated or
ranged. MEASURED, at values these refusals ADMIT:
  OPT_LR=1e30              builds, AdamW takes lr=1e+30, lr_at returns an ordinary-looking grid,
                           three maybe_step calls all report stepped=True with no alarm anywhere,
                           and the base parameters read -5.999999901390138e+28 -- FINITE, so every
                           isfinite check in this tree passes over a destroyed run.
  OPT_WEIGHT_DECAY=1e30    non-finite parameters on step 2, THROUGH a finite step 1 of
                           -1.9999999124047052e+25.
  OPT_GRAD_CLIP=1e30       accepted; the same cap that cannot bite that +inf was.
  TOK_DROPOUT=1.0          INSIDE the declared interval, admitted, and MEASURED to do exactly what
                           +inf does: size 399 not 512, bytes_per_token 1.0 not 3.5925925925925926,
                           tok.dropout_skip 3999 of 4000, and two successive regularized calls
                           returning the IDENTICAL segmentation. `stream.random()` draws from
                           [0.0, 1.0), so every draw is below 1.0.
Every one of those four is named in the refusal text or in the declaration comment beside it. A
declared per-lever domain is the general answer and is the owner's open question.

Every base parameter was -inf after ONE step while build() returned an ordinary Horizon and counters() a full ledger. findings.detail: THE max/min-STYLE HAZARD THE BRIEF NAMED, CONFIRMED IN BOTH HALVES. Clipping is a comparison against a threshold and every comparison with NaN is False, so `if clip > 0.0:` in maybe_step never entered: clipping was SILENTLY OFF at measured gradient norms of 8000000.0, with opt.clip.applied 0 AND opt.clip.armed_no_clip 0 -- neither of the two DID IT FIRE counters moving, because the branch that writes both was never reached. opt.grad_norm.p50/p99 read 8000000.0/8000000.0, which is the honest half. THE REPORT WAS THE DAMAGE: counters() built Gate('opt.build.grad_clip', clip > 0.0, clip if clip > 0.0 else 'off (0.0)', ...), so at nan the gate rendered value='off (0.0)' with the hardcoded reason "OPT_GRAD_CLIP=0.0 is OFF, which is the setting every recorded number in this project was taken under" -- while the very next gate in the same ledger interpolated the real value and printed "OPT_GRAD_CLIP=nan is OFF". TWO FIXES: the non-finite refusal closes nan at startup, and the gate's literal is replaced by the interpolated value in BOTH the value and the reason, so a report can no longer assert a setting the operator did not type.

findings.detail: ESTABLISHED WHAT THE BPE-DROPOUT PATH DOES AT inf: EVERY MERGE IS DROPPED. Every guard in the package is `dropout > 0.0`, which +inf passes, and the draw is `stream.random() < dropout`, always true at inf -- measured tok.dropout_skip 3999 over 4000 bytes. The vocabulary landed at 399 instead of 512 with tok.build_refused 143, and bytes_per_token was MEASURED AT 1.0 instead of 3.5925925925925926: that single float is the one estimator that leaves this package, and spine/derive.py::signature_width_bytes turns it into SIG's ONE window width for the whole run while DATA's splice gate reads it too. AND IT UNDOES THE RECORDED HISTORY THROUGH THE VALUE RATHER THAN THROUGH THE STREAM: at inf two successive tokenize(regularize=True) calls returned the IDENTICAL 4000 ids -- the exact 'identical segmentation on every call' symptom the child stream tok.dropout.mint was minted to repair -- because a skip probability of infinity is not random. THE STREAM AND ITS MINT SITE ARE UNTOUCHED by this work. At nan the comparison never fires (`nan > 0` is False, so no stream is attached) and the whole run is BIT-IDENTICAL to TOK_DROPOUT=0.0 with tok.dropout_skip ABSENT, which tok/api.py::tokenize's own convention reads as 'unreachable' -- the report says the regularizer is off on a run the operator switched on. TWO REFUSALS: non-finite over all four TOK float levers, and TOK_DROPOUT outside [0.0, 1.0] (the DECLARED domain -- units.PROBABILITY, 'Probability of skipping an available merge'), written as an inverted chain. NOT CLOSED and named in both the refusal and the declaration: TOK_DROPOUT=1.0 is inside the interval, admitted, and measured to do the identical damage.

findings.detail: ESTABLISHED FIRST WHETHER 0 IS A DECLARED SENTINEL HERE, BECAUSE REFUSING ONE WOULD BREAK A WORKING MECHANISM. It is not. The five TOK levers that DO carry a zero sentinel spell it out in their own help string or comment -- freeze_at '0 means never freeze', retok_every '0 leaves already-emitted ids alone forever', mint_pmin '0 mints on frequency alone', mint_novel '0 reproduces plain most-frequent minting', probation_uses 'THE DEFAULT 0 MEANS OFF'. max_bytes declares the OPPOSITE: 'The longest byte string a single token may stand for; a candidate merge longer than this is refused', implemented in Vocabulary._add as `len(seq) > self.max_bytes`. So 0 is not 'no cap', it is a cap that refuses EVERYTHING. IT DOES NOT HANG AND DOES NOT REFUSE: it builds an EMPTY vocabulary -- the 256 raw bytes, tok.build_mint 0, tok.build_refused 143, bytes_per_token 1.0 -- which is TOK_MODE=bytes reached by deleting the mint instead of by asking for it, while TOK_MODE still reads 'online' and the ledger still prints its build passes. 1 DOES EXACTLY THE SAME THING and is in the refusal with it: a merge joins two units, so the shortest sequence _add can ever be offered is two bytes long. Refused `< 2` at the first read. Nothing an operator can ask for is lost: 2 is legal and is the smallest vocabulary this package has that still mints anything.
